Title: 'My ears were ringing': Fierce storm leaves trail of damage in Damansara Damai
Article:
PETALING JAYA: A resident of Pangsapuri Saujana in Damansara Damai was left shaken after a storm struck the area yesterday, damaging his car when a tree branch fell on it.
"My ears were ringing from the sound of the extremely strong winds, followed by thunder. I was too afraid to leave my home," said Mazlan Ismail, 59.
He said the incident occurred at about 1pm, after the weather had initially been calm before the sky suddenly darkened and strong winds swept through the area.
As soon as the storm subsided, he rushed to the parking area and found his car's windows shattered, while the roof and sides of the rear boot were badly dented after being struck by the fallen branch.
"This is the second time in 3 years that we have experienced a storm this strong," he said when met at the scene.
The situation was reportedly worse in nearby areas, particularly at Pangsapuri Impian, where several residents' vehicles were damaged by fallen trees.
Residents also raised concerns over what they claimed was a lack of regular maintenance of trees along roadsides.
Pangsapuri Suria resident Rafizan Ramli, 40, said the large trees in the densely populated residential area had not been properly maintained.
"Most of the trees along the roadside have grown too large and dense, while some appear to be in poor condition.
"There has been no regular maintenance. When a strong storm hits, this is what happens.
"We urge the authorities to learn from this incident and immediately trim trees that pose a risk before someone loses their life," he said.
Rafizan said fallen trees also blocked several major roads, causing severe traffic congestion.
"Help took some time to arrive as responders had to find routes that were still accessible. However, we are grateful that the Civil Defence Force, the Fire and Rescue Department and local authorities acted quickly," he said.
Checks at the scene found that tree-cutting and debris-clearing operations were still underway to clear affected roads and ease traffic congestion.

Title: Sabah to act on Mengalum Island tourist death if safety breaches found
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government will take necessary action if any regulatory or safety violations are established following an investigation into the death of a Chinese tourist at Mengalum Island on Sept 23.
State Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said the ministry would coordinate with relevant agencies to verify the compliance status of the operator, vessel, tourism activities and facilities involved in the incident.
"We must therefore allow the police investigation to establish the circumstances and cause of death.
"At this stage, it would be premature to link the incident to the status of any licence, land, Temporary Occupation Licence (TOL), structure or facility when no such connection has been established by the investigating authorities," he said in a statement.
Jafry said the verification would cover whether the relevant licences and approvals were valid, required safety procedures had been followed, adequate safety equipment was available, safety briefings had been provided, sufficient supervision was in place and emergency response procedures had been observed.
He added that, according to police, the Chinese woman, in her 30s, was among 17 tourists who travelled to Mengalum Island and had been snorkelling for about 15 minutes in waters about 1.5 metres deep when a boat crew member monitoring the group noticed her floating unconscious.
She was brought ashore and given resuscitation but did not respond and was later pronounced dead.
Police forensic personnel found no indication of foul play at the scene, while statements had been recorded from witnesses and the case was classified as sudden death.
Jafry said regulatory matters involved several agencies, with tour operating and travel agency licensing under the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry (MOTAC), while vessel and maritime requirements, local authority approvals and land matters fell under the respective authorities.
He also said questions over the land and TOL status at Mengalum Island must be verified against official records before any conclusion could be made.
"The Sabah Government Gazette records that 3.786 hectares of State Land on Mengalum Island was declared a reserve for preservation and conservation purposes under Section 28 of the Land Ordinance.
"However, the existence of this reserve does not by itself establish the legal status of the particular site, landing point or tourism facilities involved in the September 23 incident," he said.
Jafry said any violation or non-compliance established after the investigation would be dealt with by the relevant enforcement authority in accordance with the law.
"If any violation or non-compliance is subsequently established, I expect the authority with the relevant enforcement jurisdiction to take appropriate action in accordance with the law," he said.
He added that the incident should also prompt authorities and industry players to review enforcement, operator compliance, marine safety and emergency response.
"Our responsibility is to establish what happened, determine whether all applicable requirements were complied with, and take corrective action wherever necessary," he said.
Jafry also extended his condolences to the family of the deceased, describing the loss of a visitor to Sabah as deeply regrettable.

Title: 'Malays are not immigrants', says academic
Article:
MELAKA: Malays should not be labelled immigrants in the Malay Archipelago, particularly in Tanah Melayu, as their history is closely linked to the centuries-old merantau tradition, said International Institute of Islamic Thought and Civilisation, International Islamic University Malaysia (ISTAC-IIUM) director Prof Datuk Dr Ahmad Murad Merican.
He said describing Malays as immigrants was inaccurate as it failed to take into account the history, culture and geographical ties of communities across the region.
He said the movement of Malay communities between regions in the Malay Archipelago should be understood as part of the merantau tradition, rather than migration viewed solely through the lens of modern political borders.
"Malays in Malaysia, Sumatra and Borneo are not an immigrant phenomenon but a merantau phenomenon. Among the groups that also have a merantau tradition are the Cham people. We must not be constrained by political borders, by false borders," he said.
He said the merantau tradition also connected Malay communities from various regions, including Luzon, Sumatra and Sulawesi, which share historical, cultural and linguistic ties, as well as the concept of balik kampung, referring to returning to one's place of origin and community networks.
Ahmad Murad said this when he appeared as a panellist at a session discussing 'Unravelling the Polemic of Tanah Melayu' at Musyawarah Nasional 3.0 at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC), Ayer Keroh, here today.
Musyawarah Nasional 3.0 was officiated by Deputy Prime Minister and Musyawarah Nasional founder Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, and was also attended by Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
Meanwhile, constitutional and public law expert Associate Professor Datuk Dr Shamrahayu A. Aziz said the term and status of Tanah Melayu had never disappeared as claimed by some parties, but remained enshrined in the Federal Constitution as the supreme law of the country.
"The Constitution is the law that created our country, formed and built our country, and guides how we live as a nation.
"Therefore, the name Tanah Melayu is not an issue that needs to be polemicised. We also do not know why, or the intention or motive, for saying that Tanah Melayu has disappeared," she said.
She said Tanah Melayu was referred to in the Constitution through two main terms, namely the 'States of Malaya' (Negeri-negeri Tanah Melayu) and the 'Malay Peninsula' (Semenanjung Tanah Melayu).
She said appreciating and understanding all provisions enshrined in the Constitution could increase understanding of the country's foundations and help defend the country's position.

Title: 'Stop glorifying bullying': Asyraf Wajdi urges media ban following hostel student death
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: All forms of drama and films depicting bullying that could risk triggering a "copycat" culture among youths should be stopped, said Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
He said such content could encourage youths to imitate the behaviour and portray themselves as kapla, taiko or otai.
"Stop all forms of drama or films that indirectly promote bullying in the name of 'lessons', which eventually lead to 'copycat' behaviour among youths who portray themselves as kapla, taiko, otai and others," he said in a statement on Facebook today.
The statement is believed to be in reference to the death of a Form 2 student at a secondary school in Kuala Pilah, Negri Sembilan, who was reported to have died yesterday.
The matter was shared by a woman who claimed to be the victim's aunt in several posts on Threads since last night.
Muhammad Idlan Fareeq Shahril Shahriul, 14, was reportedly found unconscious at his school hostel before being taken to Hospital Tuanku Ampuan Najihah (HTAN) in Kuala Pilah, where he was pronounced dead.
The body was later taken to the Forensic Medicine Department at Hospital Tuanku Ja'afar, Seremban, for a post-mortem.
Meanwhile, Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said police had opened an investigation under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
He said a 16-year-old boy had so far been detained to assist investigations into the incident.

Title: #NSTViral: 'If it's not enough, come and see me'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A school canteen worker's simple act of kindness towards a student from a financially struggling family has touched Malaysians after her gesture was shared on social media.
According to a Threads post by user @kalaivanirajagopal, the boy would often spend recess sitting behind the computer lab, sometimes without anything to eat.
That changed when the canteen worker, known as Kak Zira, noticed him and began giving him free food every day.
During the school's Cooperative Day, she went a step further by giving the boy money so he could buy something and enjoy the celebration with his friends.
"If it's not enough, come and see me," Kak Zira told him.
Kalaivani said the gesture was a powerful reminder that kindness did not need recognition.
"She didn't see his background. She simply saw a little boy who deserved to eat, to be happy and to feel included.
"Sometimes, the most beautiful lessons about unity aren't taught in classrooms. They happen quietly, through little acts of kindness that leave the biggest impact.
"This is the Malaysia I am proud of," said Kalaivani.
View on Threads
The heartwarming post drew praise from netizens, with many applauding Kak Zira for helping the boy without making him feel different or embarrassed.
User @coconxdh said: "Be the reason someone keeps pushing through even during tough times. I see three beautiful souls; two in the picture and one who honoured them through this writing."
Another user said: "He must be a good kid. I'm talking about good manners. Usually, women tend to melt when they meet a child who is well-mannered and respectful."
Another user wrote: "I could tell he was a good kid just by looking at him. Thank you, Kak Zira."

Title: 280 Titiwangsa students receive RM1,000 education aid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 280 tertiary students from the Titiwangsa parliamentary constituency have received RM1,000 each in financial assistance to help meet their educational needs.
The assistance was presented by Titiwangsa member of parliament Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani today.
Johari, who is also Investment, Trade and Industry Minister, said the annual assistance was aimed at helping students from low-income families pursue higher education.
He said the programme had been running since 2013, with this year's aid going to students who had newly enrolled at institutions of higher learning.
"If we want to break the cycle of poverty from one generation to the next, we cannot overlook the importance of a good education, whether at the primary, secondary or tertiary level.
"Education is very important and if we can place greater emphasis on education, it can change everything, provided it is pursued with determination," he said after the event.
On the decision to provide cash assistance instead of laptops, Johari said the approach gave students the flexibility to use the money according to their individual educational needs.
Newly enrolled Maritime Management student at Universiti Kuala Lumpur Malaysian Institute of Marine Engineering Technology in Lumut, Muhammad Zikrullah Husaini Zuber Putera, 24, said the assistance would help ease his parents' financial burden in purchasing a new laptop for his studies.
"I want to buy a new laptop and I am grateful that the assistance will, to some extent, ease the burden on my parents," he said.
Luqmanul Hakim Daswarman, 24, who is pursuing a Business Administration programme at UniKL Business School, said he planned to save the money before using it to purchase a new laptop.
"This assistance is very helpful and I am grateful to receive RM1,000. I may save the money first before using it to buy a new laptop," he said.
Nor Nadhira Abd Hadi, 32, who is pursuing Psychology at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, said the assistance would help cover part of her tuition fees.
"I will use the money to pay my tuition fees. At least it can help cover some of the costs," she said.
Earlier, Johari also visited and officiated the Malurians Fun Day Carnival 2026 at Sekolah Kebangsaan Taman Maluri here.
During the visit, he spent time engaging with the Maluri community through various activities organised for the event.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Heavy rain triggers flash floods, traffic chaos in KL, Selangor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Several areas in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor were hit by flash floods and traffic disruptions following heavy rain and thunderstorms this afternoon.
The Department of Irrigation and Drainage's Infobanjir portal showed alert-level readings at three monitoring stations in Segambut as of 5.30pm, while the Batu station also recorded an alert-level reading.
The portal also recorded moderate hourly rainfall intensity at four stations in Segambut and one in Bukit Bintang.
Among the areas affected were Damansara, Taman Tun Dr Ismail, Segambut, Kajang, Bangi, Bandar Seri Putra and Bukit Mahkota.
Several roads in Damansara and Segambut were inundated, causing traffic congestion, while the route from Bukit Mahkota towards Nilai 3 was also affected by rising floodwaters.
The Kuala Lumpur Command & Control Centre (KLCCC) reported several traffic disruptions linked to the heavy rain.
At 4.08pm, heavy rain around Kuala Lumpur resulted in congestion along Jalan Damansara and Jalan Kinabalu.
[[nid:1541701]]
Astro Radio Traffic also reported congestion on several major routes in the capital following a fallen tree and flash floods.
The fallen tree was reported on Jalan Istana near the Jalan Syed Putra exit, affecting traffic from the Sungai Besi Expressway (Besraya) and Jalan Sungai Besi towards Jalan Damansara.
Flash floods were also reported along Jalan Kuching near Petron towards Batu Caves following heavy rain, resulting in congestion from the Kepong roundabout.
Motorists were advised to exercise caution and plan their journeys accordingly.

Title: Karnival Jom Heboh gives Sarawak entrepreneurs platform to reach wider market
Article:
MIRI: Karnival Jom Heboh (KJH) is more than an entertainment event, providing entrepreneurs with an opportunity to showcase their products to thousands of visitors, said Sarawak Deputy Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development Minister Datuk Dr Ripin Lamat.
He said the participation of entrepreneurs and agencies through exhibition booths at KJH allowed them to promote their products, build networks and expand their businesses.
"We can see various booths by entrepreneurs and agencies taking part in the exhibition. This is a good opportunity for entrepreneurs to introduce their products, especially those who want to take their businesses further.
"At the same time, it can also inspire those interested in becoming entrepreneurs in the future," he said when met during a visit to the KJH exhibition booths in Miri today.
Ripin said large-scale events such as KJH also allowed entrepreneurs to interact directly with visitors, enabling them to introduce their products and services to a wider market.
Held at Miri Boulevard, KJH features entertainment activities, exhibitions and entrepreneur participation, with about 160 booths and an expected attendance of up to 300,000 visitors throughout the carnival.
The carnival has returned to Miri after several years, bringing together entertainment, community activities and business opportunities.
Besides attracting visitors, KJH provides entrepreneurs and traders with opportunities to promote their products, attract new customers and expand their business networks.

Title: Nepal missing Malaysians cannot be presumed dead after a month: Penang mufti
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians missing in Nepal following landslides and floods along the Nepal-Tibet border cannot automatically be presumed dead simply because they have remained uncontactable for a month, said Penang Mufti Associate Professor Datuk Dr Mohd Sukki Othman.
He said under Islamic law, they fell under the category of al-mafqud — people who have gone missing, are out of contact and whose status as alive or dead cannot be established with certainty.
He said the guiding principle was that "certainty cannot be removed by doubt".
"Since they were known to be alive, their status cannot be changed to deceased based merely on assumptions, as long as there is no strong evidence or confirmation from the authorities.
"However, this case differs from an ordinary missing-person case, as they disappeared in a major disaster that clearly posed a threat to their lives.
"This factor can certainly be taken into account by the authorities and the courts in deciding based on the evidence and actual circumstances," he said when contacted.
Sukki said the missing Malaysians could not be categorised as deceased because Islamic law takes a cautious approach in matters involving life, marriage, inheritance and a person's rights.
He said there was no specific period agreed upon by all fuqaha (Islamic jurists) for a missing person to be automatically declared dead.
"That is why one month alone cannot be considered conclusive proof of death.
"This is especially so as the government has previously reported that search efforts were continuing, while DNA samples from relatives of 55 Malaysians had also been obtained to assist with identification if required," he said.
Sukki said families of those missing should cooperate fully with the authorities in search and identification efforts, including by providing travel records, last known locations, photographs, medical information and DNA samples when required.
"Do not make your own decision that a family member has died until there has been proper confirmation," he said.
Sukki said once search efforts had reached a certain stage and the available evidence had been comprehensively assessed, the government should coordinate action among all relevant parties.
He said this should include religious authorities and judicial institutions so that the status of those missing could be determined according to the law and Islamic principles.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Families of missing Malaysians in Nepal to meet Wisma Putra officials tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Families of 55 Malaysians still unaccounted for following the Aug 26 glacial flash floods in Nepal will meet  Wisma Putra officials tomorrow, seeking answers over the search for their loved ones.
This comes after more than a month of uncertainty, with the families seeking clearer information on what happened at Nepal's Rasuwagadhi-Kerung border area, where some of the missing Malaysians were believed to have been last seen.
Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the families appreciated the government's efforts, including the deployment of the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) and diplomatic engagement led by Wisma Putra, but wanted greater clarity over developments on the China-Tibet side as well.
"Our concern is not about the dedication or professionalism of SMART personnel, but whether the operation was carried out at the right time, based on the right priorities and whether the areas identified by the families were thoroughly searched," he told the New Straits Times.
SMART's 11-member team was deployed to Nepal on Sept 5 and conducted ground searches and drone surveillance in areas approved and deemed safe by the Nepalese authorities before returning to Malaysia on Sept 14.
Wisma Putra had said SMART's return did not mean efforts to establish the status of the 55 Malaysians had ended.
The Nepalese authorities will continue the search, verification and identification efforts while Malaysia maintained diplomatic engagement with the relevant authorities.
"Tomorrow's meeting will involve representatives from SMART, police, Chemistry Department, Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu and National Registration Department (JPN)," he said.
Dr Manivannan is among the next-of-kin whose younger sister, Komathi, 48 is among the
55 Malaysians still missing
after the glacier floods in Nepal on Aug 26.
The families are also seeking representation from the Malaysian Embassy in Beijing, Bank Negara Malaysia and the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) at the meeting tomorrow.
He said the families also wanted the embassy in Beijing to explain Malaysia's engagement with Chinese authorities on search and recovery efforts, identification and last-known-location information, saying this would compliment the technical briefing expected from the Chemistry Department.
"The families are also seeking guidance from Bank Negara Malaysia and the AGC on the financial and legal implications of having a family member remain missing, including matters involving loans, insurance, bank accounts, property, business interests, assets and succession".
Dr Manivannan said the requests were intended to address practical problems faced by families after more than a month of uncertainty.
"This is not an additional demand for the sake of having more agencies at the table. These requests arise from specific information gaps and practical issues that the families are now facing," he said.
The meeting follows the first formal Government engagement with affected families on Day 5 (Aug 30), although not all families were represented then.
It also comes after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim spoke with Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Sept 22 and
raised the need for a formal mechanism
to assist families should the Malaysians remain unaccounted for.
Anwar had said Shah had assured him that search efforts would continue despite increasingly difficult conditions on the ground.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Fly faster': AirAsia pilot beats drone delay, unaware of passenger's desperate viral plea
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An AirAsia pilot unknowingly helped fulfil a passenger's desperate hope that her sister would make it back in time to bid their late grandmother a final farewell.
Koh Yew Weng, 37, better known as Eric, was piloting flight AK5135 from Kota Kinabalu to Kuala Lumpur at 6am on Tuesday when a woman posted a plea on social media asking the captain to fly faster so her sister could attend the funeral before the burial.
Eric only discovered the post after landing back in Kota Kinabalu later that day.
"I never expected a coincidence like this could happen. I did not know about the post when we took off.
"I only saw it after landing back in Kota Kinabalu. Only then did I understand what had happened," he said when contacted today.
The flight had faced the possibility of operational delays after drone activity disrupted runway operations at Kota Kinabalu International Airport that morning.
Air traffic control had to operate the airport's single runway in reverse, with one direction used for take-offs and the other for landings.
Eric said he and his co-pilot had initially anticipated significant delays due to the runway constraints.
"However, we were able to push back earlier despite heavy rain at the time. So, despite the runway restrictions, we did not experience long departure delays," he said.
The flight's smooth departure allowed the passenger to arrive in Kuala Lumpur on schedule, as her family had hoped.
"I have been a pilot for 10 years, and while various things have happened throughout that time, this incident stands out as a touching coincidence.
"When we were flying the aircraft, we had no idea someone was desperately hoping the flight would not be delayed," he said.
Eric said he was merely carrying out his duty and was thankful everything went smoothly, particularly after learning that the passenger had made it in time to see her grandmother's remains.
Earlier, Threads user @mierazatie posted a plea addressed to the captain of flight AK5135, hoping the aircraft would arrive promptly so her sister could see their grandmother before the burial.
Hours later, Eric replied to the post, confirming that he was the captain who operated the flight and expressing hope that her sister would make it in time.
The woman later shared that her sister had arrived in time and managed to kiss their grandmother one last time.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM18.23mil hostel complex boosts SMK Majakir capacity to 300 students
Article:
PAPAR: A new RM18.23 million hostel complex at SMK Majakir here has been completed, increasing the school's accommodation capacity from 160 to 300 students.
Papar member of parliament Datuk Armizan Ali said the project, completed on April 30, was handed over by the Sabah Education Department (JPNS) to the Papar District Education Office (PPD) today.
He said the project was particularly important for students living far from the school who depended on hostel accommodation as daily commuting was difficult.
"The old hostel could only accommodate 160 students, comprising 80 boys and 80 girls.
"However, the building was originally designed as classrooms and administrative facilities before being converted into a hostel to meet students' accommodation needs," he said in a statement today.
The new complex comprises two two-storey hostel blocks, warden houses, dormitories for students with disabilities, common rooms, isolation rooms, warden offices and reception rooms.
It also includes two sports courts, a hostel supervisor's office and a dining hall that can accommodate up to 300 people.
Armizan said the old hostel would be considered for conversion back into classrooms, providing the school with additional learning space.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Joachim: PBS to remain with GRS, strengthen multiracial identity
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Parti Bersatu Sabah (PBS) will continue working with Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) while strengthening the party as a modern, multiracial and integrity-driven political entity, said its president Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam.
He said the new PBS leadership would be guided by three main pillars — unity, stability and integrity — in line with the theme of the 41st PBS Congress held today.
"We may have different views and approaches, but our goal remains the same: to strengthen PBS and fight for Sabah's future," he said in his presidential policy speech at the congress here.
He said the struggle to uphold the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) was not over, with PBS committed to playing an active role in defending Sabah's rights and interests.
"This means our struggle is still a long one. PBS will continue to be an active, relevant and consistent voice in defending Sabah's rights and interests.
"We do not want MA63 to merely become a political slogan; we want tangible implementation and results that the people can feel," he said.
On unity, Joachim said PBS needed to remain a political home that united Sabahans regardless of race, religion, district or background.
He said the party would strengthen public participation by increasing the participation of Malays and Muslim Bumiputera, regaining the confidence of the Chinese community, and providing greater opportunities for professionals, women and the younger generation.
"PBS does not belong to one race. PBS belongs to everyone who believes in the struggle for Sabah," he said.
On GRS, he said PBS would continue to be a loyal, constructive and principled partner in the coalition.
Joachim said the party's loyalty to GRS did not mean it would lose its identity, adding that PBS would continue to voice Sabah's interests, including MA63, rural development, education, the economy, employment opportunities and the people's well-being.
"We are with GRS, but we remain PBS. In terms of integrity, positions in PBS are not a gift but a trust that requires leaders to work, go to the ground, listen to the people's problems and seek solutions," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Damai Perdana residents anxious over uncertain return home
Article:
CHERAS: Residents of Damai Perdana affected by a recent landslide are growing anxious over the lack of a clear timeline for when they can safely return home.
Currently staying at the Taman Desa Baiduri multipurpose hall temporary relief centre, they said they had been told the evacuation would last a week, but had received no firm updates on the safety of their homes or the progress of slope repairs.
S. Sossilan, 69, said the uncertainty had made it difficult for him and his wife to plan their daily routines.
"We do not even know how many days this will take. This makes things very hard for us. If they give us a clear timeframe of one, two or three weeks, we can prepare ourselves and feel at ease.
"Right now, we are sitting here not knowing how long we have to wait or when repair works will even start. We just want to return as soon as possible because being in our own home is far more comfortable," he said.
Sossilan said there had also been no discussions on temporary rental accommodation should the evacuation be extended.
Residents living near the slope at the Bandar Damai Perdana apartments were ordered to evacuate following a landslide on Tuesday.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the landslide was believed to have been triggered by a leaking underground water pipe.
He said the affected slope was about 4.57 metres high, with the landslide occurring within 0.91 metres of the affected area.
Another resident, private-sector employee Mohd Ramli Talib, 55, said the Joint Management Body (JMB) had informed residents that it had received quotations from contractors to repair the burst pipe.
However, he said no decision had been made on the appointment of a contractor or when repair works would begin.
"The problem is we do not know when the repairs will begin. If it really takes a week, we can bear staying here. But if it is suddenly extended by another two weeks, we will be at a loss.
"We need clear answers regarding the progress and time required for the repair works," he said.
[[nid:1541634]]
He said communication had also been poor, with the JMB WhatsApp group largely inactive, forcing residents to rely on neighbours and media reports for updates.
"We have not received a single piece of direct information. We were only given a notice to vacate. Key details on when repairs will start or how long they will take are completely absent.
"So we are relying on news outlets or residents from unaffected blocks.
"Our only hope is to go home. The structural integrity of the house itself is perfectly fine and solid.
"Vacating was necessary solely because of the slope failure. So we had to give in and move to this relief centre," he said.
His wife, Norlaila Ayub, 49, said the lack of clarity over the repair works remained frustrating.
"Everything is good in terms of welfare, food and shelter. We just want to know the progress of the repairs and when we can go home.
"So far, we have been left guessing, with no solid answers from the relevant parties," she said.
Another resident, civil servant Fadzilah Sulaiman, 56, said no direct briefings had been held at the relief centre, prompting residents to visit the site themselves to check the conditions.
She said the displacement had also severely disrupted her ability to care for her bedridden mother-in-law.
"I thought about bringing her here, but the facility is not disabled-friendly, and our own situation remains unstable.
"Because of that, I had to temporarily send her to my child's house in Bukit Dukung. Now I have to travel back and forth from here just to check on her," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's handicraft industry records RM240mil in sales as of July
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's handicraft industry recorded RM240.3 million in sales as of July, Deputy Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Chiew Choon Man said.
He said RM230.3 million, or 96 per cent, of the total came from the domestic market, while RM10 million, or 4 per cent, was generated from international markets.
"This figure clearly shows that while our domestic market is strong, there is still significant room to expand Malaysian handicrafts in the global market.
"The handicraft industry has value that goes far beyond the beauty of its products. It generates income, creates employment opportunities, empowers communities and elevates Malaysia's identity through culture-based tourism," he said in his speech at the launch of the Malaysia International Craft Fair (MICF) 2026 today.
Also present were Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry secretary-general Datuk Shaharuddin Abu Sohot; Malaysian Handicraft Development Corporation deputy chairman Tan Sri Ong Hong Peng; and Malaysian Handicraft Development Corporation director-general Abdul Halim Ali.
On MICF 2026, Chiew said the event played a strategic role in connecting local entrepreneurs with international buyers, markets and industry partners.
The fair, which runs from Sept 26 to Oct 5, brings together 400 local and international vendors from more than 20 countries and is targeting RM20 million in sales.
"MICF 2026 demonstrates the potential of handicrafts as both a cultural asset and a competitive global industry.
"In addition, MICF 2026 serves as a strategic business-to-business platform to empower local export-ready entrepreneurs by providing access to international buyers, including those from the United States, Japan, France, the United Arab Emirates, Taiwan, South Korea, India, Vietnam, Mauritius, the Philippines, Singapore and Indonesia."
Themed "Crafting Heritage, Inspiring Tomorrow", Chiew said MICF 2026 carried an important message that heritage should not only be preserved, but also empowered to grow, innovate and compete.
"Our hope is that MICF 2026 should be more than just an exhibition. It should serve as a platform for trade, international networking and cultural diplomacy, creating more opportunities for Malaysian handicraft entrepreneurs.
"We preserve our heritage, empower our artisans and expand our markets."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah boosts efforts to attract Chinese tourists ahead of Visit Sabah 2027
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah is stepping up efforts to attract more Chinese tourists ahead of Visit Sabah 2027, Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said.
"China remains an important tourism market for Sabah.
"As we strengthen air connectivity, our destination marketing must also reach travellers through the platforms they use to discover and plan their holidays.
"More flights mean more visitors, and more visitors mean more opportunities for our tourism industry and local communities," he said.
During a week-long visit to China to promote the state and strengthen air links, Jafry and his delegation visited Chongqing, Guiyang, Anshun and Shanghai.
The visit included meetings with airlines, tourism industry players, business representatives, cultural groups and RedNote (Xiaohongshu).
Jafry said Chongqing Airlines operated three direct flights a week to Sabah, while more flights between Sabah and Shanghai would be available by year-end as China Eastern Airlines and Spring Airlines planned to increase their flight schedules.
As of press time, Kota Kinabalu also had direct scheduled air connectivity with several destinations in China, including Beijing, Guangzhou, Hangzhou and Shenzhen, as well as Hong Kong.
"A direct flight opens the door, but we must give people a reason to keep travelling.
"That is why we are bringing tourism, culture, music, media and business together.
"Better connectivity creates opportunities across our tourism industry, from hotels and tour operators to restaurants, attractions and local businesses," Jafry said.
He added that the Sabah delegation also promoted tourism, culture, music and industry exchanges, with Malaysian singer Shila Amzah taking part in the programme in Guiyang.
Visitors from China accounted for 578,681 of the 1.1 million international arrivals to Sabah in the first eight months of 2026, an increase of 21.6 per cent compared with the same period last year.
Sabah also sought to strengthen its digital presence in China, with more than 10 million searches related to the state recorded on RedNote.
Among the platform's popular Sabah-related searches were sunsets, mountains, seas and fresh seafood.
"This is a very encouraging indication for Sabah. The interest is already there, and our focus now is to turn that interest into actual visits.
"We want more Chinese travellers to experience Sabah for themselves, from our spectacular sunsets and Mount Kinabalu to our islands, fresh seafood, wildlife and diverse cultures."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah must move up value chain, produce high-value finished products: Hajiji
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah must move towards producing and exporting high-value finished products to maximise returns from its agro-food sector, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said developing and strengthening downstream activities was an important strategy to maximise value along the agro-food supply chain, while increasing the income of agro-entrepreneurs and strengthening food security.
"We need to shift towards producing downstream products with high added value.
"This will directly improve the well-being and standard of living of our farmers, growers, smallholders and fishermen by increasing the economic value of their agricultural produce," he said after officiating at the launch of the Lumi Borneo Latex Pillow here.
His speech was delivered by Sabah Agriculture, Fisheries and Food Industry Minister Datuk Jamawi Jaafar.
Hajiji said strengthening downstream activities would also create employment opportunities, particularly for local youths.
"Certainly, these downstream or processing activities will require manpower in production, packaging, logistics, marketing, quality control and other related activities.
"This will also create opportunities for local entrepreneurs to participate," he said.
Hajiji added that the Sabah government would continue to support all sectors, including the state's rubber industry, to enable them to grow while providing better returns to rubber smallholders.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police await further tests to determine cause of student's death
Article:
SEREMBAN: The cause of death of a 14-year-old boy allegedly bullied at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah remains undetermined following a post-mortem.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the post-mortem on Muhammad Idlan Fareeq Shahril was conducted at the Forensic Medicine Department of Tuanku Ja'afar Hospital (HTJ) here, beginning at 10.30am today.
"The post-mortem, conducted by HTJ forensic pathology specialist Dr Akma Nurain Fairuz Mahamad Arif, was completed at 3pm today.
"Based on the post-mortem, the cause of death could not be determined at this time and we are still awaiting the results of further tests," he said when contacted today.
Alzafny said 21 people, including students, teachers and the victim's parents, had so far had their statements recorded to assist in the investigation.
Earlier, media reported that the Form Two student at a secondary school in Kuala Pilah died last night, allegedly after being bullied at the school hostel.
The teenager was reportedly found unconscious at the hostel before being taken to Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital (HTAN) here, where he was pronounced dead.
Alzafny was reported as saying that police had detained a 16-year-old boy to assist in the investigation and opened a probe under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
The teenager has been remanded for six days from today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Abang Johari warns against race-based politics in Sarawak
Article:
KUCHING: Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg has warned political parties against playing on emotions or adopting race-based policies in the new era.
He said such an approach could leave certain communities excluded from the state's overall development.
He said sentiment- and emotion-driven approaches should be avoided as a community's success today no longer depended on racial background, but on people's ability to contribute to development.
"If our politics is based on one race, it excludes other communities because there is no confidence as they only look towards their own group," he said when speaking at the Sarawakku Sayang 2026 programme at the Betong Sports Complex in Betong today.
Abang Johari urged Sarawakians to reflect on the state's political experience in 1987 and ensure that such an episode was not repeated.
"We must remain vigilant and ensure Sarawak moves forward towards 2030 with policies that encompass all races," he said.
The 1987 episode referred to the Sarawak political crisis, also known as the Ming Court Affair, which stemmed from a political split after a group of leaders and 27 state assemblymen challenged then chief minister Tan Sri Abdul Taib Mahmud.
The crisis led to the dissolution of the state legislative assembly and a state election in April 1987, in which BN retained the state administration.
Abang Johari said the inclusive principles of the Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) government were also reflected in Sarawak's higher education policies by providing opportunities for people of all races to pursue university studies.
He said the government was prepared to bear the high cost of ensuring these opportunities were available to all groups, with about RM200 million needed to support about 8,000 new students each year.
"Bumiputera and non-Bumiputera have equal opportunities. That means we are inclusive," he said.
Abang Johari said if opportunities and development were focused solely on one race, it could create a divided society and reduce interaction and cooperation between communities.
"If we focus only on Malays, then only Malays; Iban, only Iban, there will be no engagement and interaction between races.
"In the context of Sarawak, we give all Sarawakian children the opportunity to receive an education, develop expertise and subsequently contribute to the state's development," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM1.15m gone: Female farmer falls for love scam, fake gold investment
Article:
KUANTAN: A farmer lost over RM1.15 million after falling victim to a love scam syndicate.
Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the victim, a 50-year-old woman, befriended an individual named Siew Gui Lim @ Jason via WhatsApp on July 17 before their relationship grew closer.
"The suspect then posed as a cybersecurity consulting director and offered a gold investment, promising the victim profits.
"After the victim made payments linked to the investment, the suspect introduced a platform called 'Veniec Lottery,' claiming it was an effort to recover the invested money," he said in a statement today.
He said the victim was persuaded to make several deposits to obtain profits and bonuses, before transferring funds to seven bank accounts totaling RM1,150,034.70 from her savings and loans from family members.
"However, the victim was unable to withdraw the money and realised that she had been scammed," he said. The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
Azry Akmar advised the public not to be easily deceived by individuals who use friendship or special relationships to persuade them into making investments or handing over money.
"In addition, the public is advised to check account numbers and phone numbers through the Semak Mule platform before carrying out any financial transactions.
"Those who suspect they have become scam victims are urged to immediately contact the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) at 997 or lodge a police report," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid: BN to hold separate talks with two coalitions next week
Article:
AYER KEROH: BN will hold separate meetings with two political coalitions next week to discuss possible cooperation for the Melaka election, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
The BN chairman confirmed that the meetings would be held at the BN headquarters at World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL).
The meetings will be led by Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, together with the top leaders of the two coalitions.
However, Zahid, who is also Umno president, declined to identify the coalitions, saying discussions had yet to begin.
"Next week, the party headquarters has arranged two separate meetings involving two different groups on different dates and at different times.
"Through these negotiations, we must look at what is harmful and what is reasonable, and ultimately, as a political coalition under the name of BN, we want to look at the benefits to the country and, in particular, our coalition, in the medium and long term," he said.
He said this after officiating the National Musyawarah: "Unravelling the Tanah Melayu Land Polemic" at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here today.
Also present were Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Chief Minister, and National Musyawarah chairman Tan Sri Abd Ghani Othman.
Asked whether BN would negotiate with only one of the component parties of Perikatan Nasional (PN) following the Registrar of Societies (RoS) suspension of all coalition activities, Zahid, who is also Deputy Prime Minister, said the matter would be left to Asyraf and PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar.
"However, we are more comfortable with a party that is at ease than with a coalition that has 'fallen apart'," he said.
Recently, Zahid gave Ab Rauf the mandate to hold discussions with any political parties interested in working with BN for the Melaka election.
He was reported as saying that any outcome or proposal for cooperation must be brought to the BN and Umno leadership for consideration before being finalised.
Ab Rauf subsequently confirmed that discussions with other political parties would begin after receiving the green light from the party's top leadership.
He said the 21 state seats won by BN in the 2021 Melaka election would form the basis of the negotiations. BN won 21 of the 28 seats in that election, with PH winning five and PN two.
A day before the Melaka state assembly dissolution took effect on Wednesday, Ab Rauf said BN Melaka had yet to decide whether to contest alone or form an alliance with another party.
He said negotiations would only be discussed after the dissolution of the state assembly.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar wants pondok education elevated, youths exposed to Islamic knowledge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants pondok education to be elevated and younger generations to be exposed to the wealth of Islamic knowledge.
He said this would ensure that progress brought greater good when guided by faith, good character and a sense of responsibility towards others.
Anwar said the history of the nation could not be separated from pondok schools and pesantren, which preserved faith, safeguarded knowledge and educated generations to maintain their identity during colonial rule.
"That is why we must continue to elevate pondok education and bring younger generations closer to the wealth of Islamic knowledge.
"No matter how quickly the world changes, progress only brings good when guided by faith, good character and a sense of responsibility towards others," he said in a Facebook post today.
The statement came after he attended the Sebarkan Salam and Pendang Berselawat programme at Pondok Mujamma' Ibnu Sunni Al-Talaqqi (Mushtaq) in Pendang, Kedah, last night.
Anwar said he was moved by the large turnout of people who came to listen to religious talks, seek knowledge and recite selawat for Prophet Muhammad.
"I chose to listen first to the advice of the religious teachers because no matter how high a person's position, we must remain humble before knowledge.
"We also need to appreciate the views of those who not only study religious texts and the scholarly heritage, but also understand the concerns of society and the challenges facing the ummah," he said.
He said the contributions of religious teachers who diligently taught despite limited resources could never be forgotten.
He said the message on wisdom and compassion at the programme was also close to his heart, as Islam required Muslims to uphold justice firmly and safeguard their trust.
"However, firmness must always be accompanied by compassion so that knowledge makes us more honest, more courteous when we disagree and more aware of the hardships faced by others.
"May Allah SWT guide us to become a people whose faith is steadfast, whose knowledge is broad, whose character is noble and who always bring mercy to society," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar reaffirms commitment to Malays, Bumiputeras while protecting others' rights
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has reaffirmed his commitment to protecting the interests of Malays and Bumiputeras while stressing that their advancement must not come at the expense of other Malaysians.
Anwar said the Bumiputera agenda could be strengthened while upholding social justice and respecting the rights and interests of non-Malays.
"I want to help the Malays because they are my people. I'm proud of their culture and heritage.
"But it's not a zero-sum game," he said in his address at the Himpunan Mesra Alumni UiTM.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said he had never supported views that insulted other communities, belittled their contributions or denied their rights.
"But I have never agreed with any view that insults others, belittles the role of others or denies the rights of others. That is my position," he said.
He said Malaysia's constitutional system provided a clear framework that must be respected by whoever led the country, including the Madani government.
"Whoever becomes a leader, especially in the Madani government, cannot dismantle or unravel the fundamental principles of our country's Constitution."
Anwar said the government would continue to prioritise Bumiputera development through policies and agencies aimed at strengthening economic, social and educational opportunities.
However, he said that the agenda should not be treated as a political contest between different groups.
"This is not one group against another. To make the Bumiputera agenda successful, we need to harness all our strengths."
Anwar also emphasised the need to ensure that funds allocated to Malay and Bumiputera agencies were properly managed and protected from abuse and misappropriation.
He said the government's approach was to strengthen the Bumiputera agenda while ensuring social justice and protecting the interests of other Malaysians.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar signals fairer bonus distribution in 2027 Budget
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was reviewing how bonuses are distributed between chief executives and lower-paid workers.
Anwar said he had encountered situations where chief executive officers (CEOs) received bonuses equivalent to eight months' salary while workers received only two months.
"I do not agree with that. I have changed this approach," he said during a question-and-answer session at the Himpunan Mesra Alumni Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) at the Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor (DATC), UiTM, here.
Anwar said if workers were given a three-month bonus, CEOs should also receive a bonus equivalent to three months.
He said the issue was part of the government's broader effort to ensure workers benefited more fairly from the performance and profits of companies.
Anwar acknowledged that CEOs who were qualified and responsible for leading companies were generally rewarded with high salaries and substantial bonuses.
However, he said the disparity between executive remuneration and workers' earnings should not be allowed to widen excessively.
He cited an example of a CEO earning RM40,000 a month while a worker involved in basic services earned RM2,000.
"Already, there is a difference in their salaries. This is also why we need to look at fairness," he said.
Anwar said the government had taken a similar approach in reforming the public service salary structure, with lower-paid civil servants receiving proportionately larger increases.
He said the principle of fairness did not necessarily mean everyone receiving the same amount, but ensuring those who needed greater support received appropriate attention.
Anwar said the approach was also important as Malaysia sought to ensure rising productivity and corporate profits translated into better living standards for workers.
He had earlier said the government remained concerned about companies recording high profits while maintaining relatively low wage levels.
Anwar said addressing the wage gap was part of the government's effort to "raise the ceiling" by promoting higher-value economic activity while also "raising the floor" by improving workers' incomes.
He said the government would announce further measures on wages when Budget 2027 is tabled on Oct 9. The 2027 Budget is scheduled to be tabled in the Dewan Rakyat at 4pm on Oct 9.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar approves RM2.5mil to upgrade UiTM Tun Arshad Ayub campus
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved RM2.5 million to upgrade the newly renamed UiTM Tun Arshad Ayub Jalan Othman campus in Petaling Jaya.
The allocation was announced by Anwar during the Himpunan Mesra Alumni UiTM here, following his declaration that the UiTM Jalan Othman campus would be renamed UiTM Tun Arshad Ayub Jalan Othman.
The campus traces its origins to Dewan Latihan RIDA, established in 1956, and is closely associated with the beginnings of UiTM.
Anwar said the allocation was part of the government's efforts to strengthen UiTM and ensure its institutions continued to provide quality educational opportunities for Bumiputera students.
He also reaffirmed the government's commitment to the Bumiputera development agenda, particularly in education, economic growth and social development.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said UiTM's operating and development allocation had increased significantly under the Madani government.
He said UiTM received RM3.08 billion in 2026, compared with less than RM2 billion before the Madani government took office.
Anwar also stressed the need for funds allocated to Malay and Bumiputera agencies to be properly managed and protected from abuse and misappropriation.
He said strengthening UiTM's capabilities was important to ensure the university continued to progress as a centre of academic excellence.
The prime minister also announced RM100,000 each for the TUNaS Belia NEET programme and the Himpunan Mesra Alumni UiTM as a show of support and appreciation for the efforts of the UiTM Malaysia Alumni Federation (PAUiTM).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Goh Sze Fei‑Nur Izzuddin storm into quarterfinals as Pearly Tan‑Thinaah sparkle with straight‑set wins
Article:
NAGOYA, Sept 26 — Malaysia’s national professional men’s doubles pair, Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani, are one step away from securing a medal at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games after advancing to the quarterfinals following a straight-set victory over Japan’s Yugo Kobayashi-Takuro Hoki today.
During the match held at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium, the national pair faced no major issues in claiming a 21-19, 21-16 straight-set win.
Waiting for the national pair in tomorrow’s quarterfinal round will be either China’s Liang Wei Keng-Wang Chang or Thailand’s Chaloempoen Charoenkitamorn-Worrapol Thongsa-nga, who are set to play in another match later today.
Meanwhile, another national men’s doubles pair, Aaron Chia and Tee Kai Wun, fell short of reaching the quarterfinals of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after bowing out to South Korea’s world number one pair, Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae, in straight sets of 21-19, 21-16.
In the women’s doubles event, Pearly Tan-M Thinaah lived up to expectations by easily defeating Thailand’s Napapakorn Tungkasatan-Hathaihip 21-8, 21-12.
The national pair is scheduled to face India’s Gayatri Gopichand-Treesa Jolly, who pulled off an upset by defeating the host country’s pair 24-22, 21-18.
In the men’s singles event, national representative Justin Hoh failed to advance to the quarterfinals after losing to Singapore’s Loh Kean Yew 21-14, 21-14. — Bernama

Title: As heavy rain and flooding continue in Bangkok, Malaysians urged to stay vigilant
Article:
BANGKOK, Sept 26 — Malaysians in Bangkok have been urged to exercise caution and remain vigilant as persistent heavy rain and flooding continue to disrupt roads and daily activities across the Thai capital, with all 50 districts declared disaster zones.
In an advisory issued Saturday, the Malaysian Embassy in Bangkok urged Malaysians residing in or travelling to the city to keep abreast of the latest weather, road, and traffic conditions and plan their journeys in advance.
“Malaysians are advised to check road and flood conditions before travelling, allow additional travel time, avoid flood-affected areas, and consider alternative routes or modes of transport where necessary,” it said.
The embassy cautioned that weather and road conditions could change rapidly, particularly in flood-affected areas, and urged Malaysians to monitor local conditions and follow advisories and instructions issued by the relevant Thai authorities.
It said the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) provides an online Road Flood Monitoring System that allows the public to check road conditions and water levels at monitoring points across the capital.
The embassy said Malaysians could also report flooding or standing water through Traffy Fondue or contact the BMA Hotline at 1555, which operates around the clock.
For travel information, assistance or enquiries, Malaysians may contact the Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) Contact Centre at 1672 or the Tourist Police at 1155.
Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt earlier declared all 50 districts in the capital disaster zones, following persistent heavy rain that caused flooding and traffic disruptions.
Flooding was reported in 93 districts, 350 sub-districts, and 1,425 villages, while waterlogging affected 44 road locations in Bangkok.
As of 7am on Saturday, flooding remained in 21 provinces nationwide, affecting 27,109 households and 84,605 people, according to the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM).
At press time, no casualties had been reported in Bangkok, although some e-hailing services had stopped accepting bookings due to road closures, while some shops remained closed. — Bernama

Title: Fama readies warehouses nationwide with buffer stocks as El Niño threat rises
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 26 — The Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama) has taken proactive steps to safeguard the nation’s food supply by establishing a special committee two months ago to prepare for the possible impact of El Nino.
Its chairman, Abang Ahmad Kerdee Abang Masagus, said the move reflected Fama’s early action to prepare for the phenomenon, including plans to procure and store agro-food products at Fama warehouses nationwide.
“At Fama, we established a committee two months ago. Although El Niño is an annual phenomenon, we took proactive measures this year instead of waiting for it to occur.
“By taking early action and coordinating with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) on when the phenomenon is expected to begin, we were able to make early preparations this year,” he told reporters here today.
He said this when met at the Penang 2026 JAM Mega programme at Lotus’s Seberang Jaya, which was officiated by Penang State Rural Development, Agrotechnology, Food Security and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Datuk Rashidi Zinol.
Previously, MetMalaysia director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip was reported as saying that there was more than a 90 per cent probability of El Niño reaching the “very strong” or “Super El Nino” category between October and December.
Abang Ahmad Kerdee said Fama also planned to purchase selected agro-food products and keep them in its warehouses as buffer stocks against potential supply disruptions, including those caused by import and export issues.
He said Fama had warehouses in every state, including cold storage facilities, which would be fully utilised to ensure sufficient food supplies.
“The stocks include around 34 types of agro-food products, including red chillies, green chillies, cabbage and onions, as well as other food products such as chicken and beef.
“Should there be any issues, such as difficulties in securing imports or exports, we have a backup plan to ensure that there is sufficient supply of these products for several months,” he said.
Abang Ahmad Kerdee said the approach drew on the country’s experience during the Covid-19 pandemic, when early planning and adequate food stocks helped maintain continuity in food supplies. — Bernama

Title: Storm clouds gather: MetMalaysia issues urgent alert for Kuala Lumpur and 12 states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur and 12 states until 8pm today.
It said in a statement that the adverse weather is forecast to affect Perlis, Terengganu, Kedah (Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Pokok Sena, Yan, Kuala Muda, Pendang, Padang Terap and Sik), as well as Penang (Seberang Perai Utara, Barat Daya and Timur Laut).
Similar weather conditions are also forecast in Hilir Perak, Bagan Datuk, Muallim, Batang Padang, Perak Tengah, Kinta, Kampar and Manjung in Perak; Pasir Puteh, Bachok, Kota Bharu, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Machang, Tanah Merah and Jeli in Kelantan.
Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Bentong, Pulau Tioman, Temerloh, Jerantut and Kuantan in Pahang; Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling and Klang in Selangor; Kuala Pilah, Tampin, Rembau and Jempol in Negeri Sembilan; and Mersing in Johor.
In Sabah and Sarawak, the affected areas are Sandakan, West Coast (Ranau, Kota Belud and Tuaran), Kudat (Kota Marudu), Tawau (Lahad Datu, Kalabakan and Kunak) and the Interior (Sipitang, Tenom, Sook, Keningau, Tambunan, Membakut and Beaufort); and Limbang, Miri (Bario and Telang Usan), Kapit (Song, Belaga and Bukit Mabong), Sibu (Kanowit), Sarikei, Kuching, Serian (Tebedu), Betong (Saratok), Samarahan, and Sri Aman (Lubok Antu). — Bernama

Title: Madani Mart’s master licensing push could fuel 300 outlets, says Fuziah
Article:
KAJANG, Sept 26 — Madani Mart is opening master licensing applications to companies, investors, and strategic partners with financial and operational capabilities to accelerate its retail network expansion nationwide.
Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said each party appointed by Yayasan Madani will have the opportunity to develop and operate up to 100 Madani Mart branches, subject to set terms and standards.
“Currently, priority will be given to three (master licensees). This means if we appoint three, it will enable the opening of around 300 outlets,” she told Bernama after opening the Madani Mart Taman Sutera branch here today.
Fuziah, who is also Yayasan Madani chairman, said the appointment and branch development rights will be awarded in phases based on capability, performance, and compliance with the conditions established by Yayasan Madani.
She said expansion through this model will begin after Yayasan Madani ensures the supply chain and pricing for about 5,000 stock-keeping units (SKUs) offered by Madani Mart remain stable.
Fuziah said Yayasan Madani is negotiating with several commercial and government-owned banks to provide financing facilities up to RM50 million if required.
She added that the master licensing model was introduced to speed expansion. Opportunities to open individual outlets are still offered to ensure more entrepreneurs can join the network.
“We still want to provide opportunities to individual owners. We do not want a situation where only a select few make a profit,” she said, adding that Madani Mart aims to have at least one branch in every state legislative assembly constituency.
Meanwhile, on the opening of Madani Mart Taman Sutera, Fuziah said the third branch introduces a fresh grocery segment, including fish and vegetables, as well as bulk sales for items that do not require specific licences.
The bulk sales facility offers small traders, food operators, and stall owners options to obtain supplies in larger quantities at competitive prices, helping manage operating costs.
To date, Madani Mart operates two locations in Kuantan, Pahang, before opening in Taman Sutera, which marks the network’s first branch in the Klang Valley.
Madani Mart is a strategic partner of the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) in executing the Rahmah Madani Sales Programme (PJRM), with every outlet hosting at least one Rahmah Sale per month and providing payment system facilities for the Rahmah Basic Contribution (SARA) programme. — Bernama

Title: Van impaled by guardrail in Kuching crash, passenger injured
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 26 — A passenger van was impaled by a roadside guardrail after crashing at a traffic light junction in Bandar Baru Samariang this morning.
See Hua Daily News
reported that the incident occurred at about 7am today.
The van is believed to have lost control before crashing into the roadside barrier, causing the guardrail to pierce through the vehicle.
The van was carrying one female passenger at the time.
She sustained injuries in the incident and received initial treatment from paramedics at the scene before being taken to Sarawak General Hospital for further treatment. — The Borneo Post

Title: Anwar questions Opposition priorities: ‘No salary, they’re angry; those who steal, they don’t mention’
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today questioned the federal Opposition’s priorities, taking a swipe at its MPs for scrutinising his refusal to draw a prime ministerial salary while, he said, saying little about those who “
sakau
”, or steal, large sums of money.
Anwar recalled being questioned by Opposition MPs in Parliament over how he could support himself without taking his salary as prime minister.
He said he had also been told by the Opposition that even Prophet Muhammad received wages, but added that he had never heard that the Prophet took a salary.
“Then I said, I don’t take a salary, but I don’t fall under the B40 category. Firstly, I take the allowance,” he said during a gathering with Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) alumni and students at the university’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor.
Anwar said the government also provides the vehicle he uses, accommodation at the prime minister’s official residence, Seri Perdana, and flights.
“It’s enough
lah
. Not rich, but not poor,” he said of his financial position.
He then questioned what the Opposition had chosen to focus on.
“But they want to ‘
sibuk
’ [interfere], want to be angry. Don’t take a salary, they’re angry. Those who ‘
sakau
’ [steal] a lot, they don’t mention,” he said, drawing laughter from the audience.
Anwar did not elaborate on whom he was referring to in his remarks about the Opposition.
Last month, Anwar also used the word “
sakau
” when speaking about alleged past financial mismanagement at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), following the government’s July 29 release of a Royal Commission of Inquiry report into the pilgrims’ fund.
The RCI examined TH’s management and operations from 2014 to 2020. The government subsequently said investigations based on the report’s findings would proceed and that action would be taken if breaches of the law were established.
In 2024, PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang reportedly suggested in the Dewan Rakyat that Anwar was seeking to appear more pious than Prophet Muhammad by refusing to accept a salary.
Anwar has declined to draw his salaries as prime minister and finance minister since taking office in November 2022, while continuing to receive his allowance as Tambun MP.
